questions: Should the function treat integer keys in the input dictionary as part of the counting, or only the integer values within the lists?

What should happen if the input dictionary values are not lists (e.g., tuples, sets, or other iterables)?

Is the order of keys in the output dictionary important (e.g., sorted by integer, by first appearance)?
Should the function raise an error if any list element is not an integer, or should it skip non-integers and only count integers?
